note: Colour confidence rules fitted on the SightBench dev split only (synthetic renders), never on test. Everything not listed under fitted.changed keeps its hand-set value from threshold_sets/initial-unfitted.json.

fitted.on: SightBench dev split only: evals/sightbench/manifests/dev.json, 180 synthetic pairs (23 colour mismatches), sha256 8cbbba4238015b03cdd9779178362366cf596ce4e0f2790d9851781489dd63bc. No model key.
fitted.goal: No "sure" colour disagreement on items whose colour is right, keeping as many colour-mismatch calls as possible.

changed.colour.quality_issue_steps: 0 -> 1. An item photo that fails the quality gate (blurry, too far, too close, too dark) lowers colour confidence one step, like dim light. On dev, all 5 "sure" disagreements on right-colour items came from such photos (3 blurry, 1 too far, 1 too close); the one sure-detectable colour swap was in a photo that passed.
changed.colour.sure_min_de_same_brightness: off -> 10. Without a white reference the exposure is unknown, so a "sure" disagreement also needs delta E >= 10 after matching the delivered colour to the listing colour's brightness. White read as grey comes out near 0. On dev, right-colour items in good light stay at or below 9.7 at matched brightness (one outlier, 14.7, in a too-close photo); navy delivered for black is 11.1.
changed.colour.poor_bright_luma: 0.15 -> 0.30. Below it the colour check says it is too dark. On dev, under 0.30 a colour disagreement carried no information: 23 of 34 right-colour items "disagreed", against 3 of 6 wrong-colour ones; above it, 19 of 64 against 5 of 9.

dev_before_after.how: evals/sightbench/run.ts --split dev against the service with each set, no model key (the runner never writes a result file for dev).
dev_before_after.sightline_mismatch_recall: 3 of 90 -> 1 of 90 (the 2 lost were model swaps flagged by a wrong "sure" colour call)

fitted.unchanged: The delta E cut-offs (12 to disagree, 25 to be sure without the colour name) still fall inside the range dev allows: right-colour items in photos that pass the quality gate, in good light, reach 10.1; the one sure-detectable swap is 12.2. The cast limits and the dim-light limit were scanned on dev and left as they were (moving them gained at most one dev pair). Name tolerances and the quality-gate, mask, label and fusion values were not refitted.
fitted.not_fixed: Wood tables and plank floors: gray-world white balance reads the orange surface as orange light and the check abstains (heavy colour cast). The masks there are fine, so this is not a mask bug; it needs a white reference in the photo.
fitted.test_outcome: Scored once on the frozen test split after fitting (evals/RESULTS.md, run 2): false alarms 6 -> 1 of 210 and false-alarm twin 45 -> 21 of 210, but mismatches flagged 7 -> 2 of 210, colour swaps 4 -> 1 of 53. The same-brightness cut held back navy for black (9.2), royal blue for navy (7.1) and black for sky blue (9.1, chroma squashed when matching to a near-black listing). Not refitted on test; the next fit needs more dev colour swaps.
